principle: Cathodic electrodeposition of gold from a Au(I)-sulfite complex — Na3[Au(SO3)2] or (NH4)3[Au(SO3)2] — in an alkaline (pH ~8-10) electrolyte with a large excess of free sulfite ligand; insoluble anodes evolve oxygen and gold is replenished from salt/concentrate. The core chemistry problem: Au(SO3)2(3-) is a WEAK complex (stability constant log beta ~10 vs ~38 for Au(CN)2-), so Au(I) is thermodynamically prone to disproportionation 3Au(I) -> 2Au(0) + Au(III): the bath spontaneously precipitates metallic gold onto tank walls, heaters and dust nuclei unless held alkaline with excess sulfite plus organic stabilizers (amines/polyamines, EDTA-class chelators, heterocycles — the proprietary heart of commercial products). Thiosulfate Au(S2O3)2(3-) is a much stronger complex (log beta ~26); mixed sulfite-thiosulfate baths exploit this to run near-neutral pH with better shelf stability at the cost of sulfur-codeposition risk. Deposits are fine-grained, low-stress, high-purity soft gold (24k class) with excellent throwing power; hardened variants use ppm-level As/Sb/Tl grain refiners or Pd/Cu alloying.

substrates: nickel-plated steel (standard stack: steel -> Ni barrier -> sulfite Au)
nickel and nickel alloys (activate before gold — Ni passivates fast in air)
copper/brass via Ni or Pd barrier (direct Au on Cu interdiffuses)
stainless steel via Wood's nickel strike
gold-flash over electroless Ni (electronics ENIG-adjacent stacks)
applicability.steel_wire_notes: Same rule as all gold plating: NEVER directly on bare steel — no adhesion (displacement effects, oxide) and Fe contamination poisons the bath. Stack for the anchor product: degrease -> electroclean -> pickle -> (Wood's Ni strike if stainless) -> Ni barrier 2-5 um -> (gold strike, see solutions) -> sulfite gold. One genuine advantage over ACID cyanide gold for steel work: the alkaline sulfite bath does not chemically attack steel the way pH 4 citrate does, so an accidental bare-steel touch is less catastrophic — but the adhesion/barrier logic is unchanged. Reel-to-reel/continuous wire operation is possible (sulfite gold is used in continuous electronics plating), though high-speed formulations are less developed than acid cyanide hard gold; moving wire provides the needed agitation. Live entry still mandatory.
applicability.non_conductive_notes: Glass/ceramic houseware: not directly platable — needs metallization first (silvering, conductive paint, electroless Ni/Cu seed); PVD is the natural glass route. Steel/brass spoons and cups: stack works; food-contact status of Ni undercoat, As-doped hardened gold (arsenic — absolute food-contact stop) and stabilizer residues [UNKNOWN — needs food-contact regulation check per market]. For food contact use only undoped high-purity gold and verify. EN 1811 nickel-release limits bind for skin-contact jewelry with Ni barrier [FACT: regulation exists].
applicability.jewelry_thickness_classes: Same class ladder as any gold plating: flash 0.05-0.175 um; 'gold plated' >=0.5 um; micron plating 1-2.5 um; heavy-wear rings 2.5-5 um. ISO 27874 jewelry gold-coating classes apply; ASTM B488 Type III (99.9% Au min, soft, 20-90 HK — Code A/B) is the matching engineering class for undoped sulfite gold [FACT: published class structure]. Sulfite gold's high purity and ductility put it in the SOFT class unless hardened.

components.name: plating tank
components.diy_notes: polypropylene/PVDF/glass. Sulfite-specific: smooth walls, no scratches/dead corners — plated-out gold nucleates on roughness; a lidded tank matters (air oxidizes sulfite).

components.name: DC rectifier / power supply
components.purpose: constant-current source 0-12 V; A = current_density x immersed dm2
components.diy_notes: bench CC supply fine; low ripple (<5%) preferred. Sulfite baths run LOW current density — a 0-3 A supply covers jewelry lots.

components.name: insoluble anode
components.purpose: O2-evolving counter-electrode; gold replenished from salt/concentrate
components.diy_notes: platinized titanium or MMO titanium [FACT: standard]. Caution: anodic oxidation destroys sulfite at the anode (SO3(2-) -> SO4(2-)) — some systems use membrane-separated anode compartments to slow ligand burn; at DIY scale accept faster sulfite replenishment instead. Never stainless anodes.

components.name: immersion heater + thermostat
components.diy_notes: quartz/Ti/PTFE lab heater, +/-2 C. Sulfite-specific: heater surface is the #1 site for gold plate-out — inspect and strip it; do not overshoot temperature (accelerates disproportionation and sulfite oxidation).

components.name: agitation (MECHANICAL, not air)
components.purpose: replenish Au at cathode boundary layer
components.diy_notes: magnetic stirrer, cathode-rod movement, or pumped eductor. AIR AGITATION IS WRONG for sulfite baths — O2 oxidizes the sulfite ligand and ages the bath [FACT: chemistry]; this is a standing difference vs acid cyanide practice.

components.name: pH meter + thermometer
components.purpose: hold pH window (8-10 sulfite class; 6-8 mixed-ligand per TDS); pH floor is a safety AND stability line
components.diy_notes: calibrated meter; raise pH with NaOH/KOH solution, lower ONLY with dilute weak acid additions per TDS — never strong acid into a sulfite bath (SO2 gas + instant gold crash).

components.name: continuous filtration (1-5 um)
components.purpose: remove gold particles from micro-disproportionation before they seed roughness and autocatalytic bath decomposition
components.diy_notes: more important than in cyanide baths: fines of metallic gold are decomposition nuclei. Small pump + PP cartridge; filter the bath even when idle if possible.

components.name: racks / barrel / reel-to-reel fixtures
components.diy_notes: Ti or plastisol-coated Cu racks; small barrel for many rings; contact rollers before the cell for continuous wire.

components.name: drag-out (dead) rinse tank
components.diy_notes: same gold-economy logic as any gold bath; recovery from sulfite drag-out is simple (gold reduces out readily — the instability becomes a recovery feature).

components.name: cool dark storage / bath rest protocol
components.purpose: sulfite baths age even unused (air oxidation, slow disproportionation)
components.diy_notes: keep lidded, cool, filtered; small-volume bath sized to actual throughput beats a big bath dying on the shelf — bath LIFE, not hardware, is the sulfite tax.

operation_sequence.action: verify bath: temperature, pH, free sulfite (iodometric titration or supplier kit), gold content, no visible gold dust/mirror on walls or heater; filtration running
operation_sequence.parameters: T 40-60 C; pH per TDS (8-10 sulfite class); free sulfite in excess per TDS
operation_sequence.failure_watch: purple/brown tint or gold film on tank = decomposition started — filter hard, correct sulfite/pH, or reclaim; pH <7 on a sulfite bath = STOP (SO2 risk + crash)

operation_sequence.action: complete pretreatment chain (see prep_chain_required) ending in fresh active Ni, rinsed, kept wet
operation_sequence.failure_watch: passive Ni (sat in air/water >1-2 min) under sulfite gold = adhesion failure; re-activate in dilute acid dip + rinse

operation_sequence.action: gold strike (see solutions: sulfite strike or main bath at strike conditions), live entry
operation_sequence.parameters: low Au strike or main bath at ~2x normal CD for 20-40 s [ESTIMATE: handbook practice, medium]
operation_sequence.failure_watch: no live entry -> immersion/displacement film -> peeling; uneven pale coverage = activation failed

operation_sequence.action: plate in main sulfite gold bath, live entry, mechanical agitation on
operation_sequence.parameters: 0.1-0.6 A/dm2 typical rack window (some decorative baths to ~1) [FACT: published typical range]; cell voltage falls where it falls, typ 1.5-4 V
operation_sequence.duration: ~2-6 min per micron at 0.3-0.5 A/dm2 given the near-100% cathode efficiency of sulfite gold [ESTIMATE: handbook-range + Faraday calc, medium-high]
operation_sequence.failure_watch: burned/brown at edges = CD too high for Au content/agitation; dull haze = organic/stabilizer imbalance; roughness = gold fines in suspension (filtration!)

operation_sequence.action: withdraw into drag-out (still) rinse, dwell and drain
operation_sequence.failure_watch: coiled wire drags badly — orient to drain; skipping = gold loss + rinse contamination

operation_sequence.action: cascade rinse, optional hot final DI rinse, warm-air dry
operation_sequence.failure_watch: sulfite residue trapped in coils dries to white salt haze — rinse interiors of wound wire well

operation_sequence.action: inspect + test per testing_acceptance before release
operation_sequence.parameters: XRF thickness, adhesion bend on coupon, color vs retained standard
operation_sequence.failure_watch: sulfite gold is SOFT — handle with plastic tweezers/tissue until any topcoat/hardening step; fingerprints and drag scratches show

solutions.solution_name: alkaline sulfite gold main bath (soft 24k class)
solutions.purpose: the standard cyanide-free gold deposit: high-purity, ductile, bright-to-satin soft gold for decorative/jewelry and electronics use

composition.hazard_class: low acute toxicity relative to KAu(CN)2 (no cyanide); irritant class; ammonium form releases NH3 at high pH/heat [FACT]

composition.hazard_class: low hazard solid; releases toxic SO2 gas on contact with acid [FACT]

composition.role: conductivity, pH buffering in the 8-10 window
composition.hazard_class: low hazard (borates: reprotoxic class in EU at high content) [FACT]

composition.role: the proprietary core: kinetically block Au(I) disproportionation, refine grain, brighten; commercial cyanide-free products live or die on this package
composition.hazard_class: [UNKNOWN — needs supplier SDS; amines typically corrosive/sensitizing class]

composition.chemical: grain refiner / hardener dopant (HARDENED VARIANT ONLY): arsenic, antimony or thallium compounds
composition.role: grain refinement raising hardness of sulfite gold from soft class toward ~120-160 HV; classic sulfite-bath hardener is arsenic-doped
composition.hazard_class: arsenic compounds: Carc. 1A, acutely toxic; thallium: acutely toxic, cumulative — HANDLE AS THE MOST HAZARDOUS SPECIES IN THE CYANIDE-FREE SYSTEM; irony: the 'safe' bath's hardener can be nastier than the bath [FACT]
composition.tag: [FACT: published practice; exact dose per supplier TDS]

operating_window.pH: 8.0-10.0 sulfite class window; NEVER below ~7 (SO2 release + gold crash); high end >10 risks some stabilizers and ammonia loss in ammonium systems [FACT: published typical range]
operating_window.current_density_A_dm2: 0.1-0.6 rack typical, up to ~1 in agitated decorative baths [FACT: published typical range]
operating_window.voltage: current-controlled; cell voltage typically 1.5-4 V at rack CD
operating_window.agitation: mechanical/cathode movement/pumped flow — NOT air (sulfite oxidation)
operating_window.deposition_rate: ~2-6 min per micron at 0.3-0.5 A/dm2 (cathode efficiency near 100% for sulfite Au — a real advantage over 30-50%-efficient acid hard gold) [ESTIMATE: handbook-range + Faraday calc, medium-high]
operating_window.anode: platinized Ti / MMO, insoluble; membrane-separated anolyte in some industrial cells to protect sulfite; replenish gold as sulfite salt/concentrate [FACT]

solutions.maintenance: Analyze and feed: Au (+/-20% of setpoint), FREE SULFITE (iodometric titration — the signature sulfite-bath analysis; sulfate accumulates as dead ballast), pH (drifts down from anodic acid generation; correct with NaOH/KOH). Filter continuously; strip plated-out gold from heater/walls before it seeds runaway decomposition. Keep lidded and cool when idle; minimize idle heating. Contamination: heavy metals (Cu, Pb, Fe) at ppm level dull/darken deposits [ESTIMATE: handbook-range, medium — exact limits per TDS]; drag-in of ACID from pickle line is the kill-shot (local pH crash -> gold precipitation + SO2) — rinse discipline before gold is stricter than in cyanide shops. Expect FINITE BATH LIFE measured in metal-turnovers well below cyanide baths; budget bath replacement/reclaim as a consumable [FACT: recognized sulfite limitation].

solutions.purpose: improved-stability cyanide-free variant: thiosulfate's stronger Au(I) complexation (log beta ~26) lets the bath run near-neutral pH with much slower spontaneous decomposition; also the basis of cyanide-free ELECTROLESS/immersion gold formulations

composition.chemical: gold added as sulfite complex (converts to mixed-ligand speciation in bath)

composition.role: primary strong ligand; enables pH 6-8 operation
composition.hazard_class: low hazard; decomposes to SO2 + colloidal sulfur on acid contact [FACT]

composition.role: co-ligand + antioxidant scavenging that suppresses thiosulfate breakdown to sulfide/sulfur
control grain and keep sulfur out of the deposit

operating_window.pH: 6.0-8.0 (the whole point of the variant) [FACT: published characteristic]
operating_window.agitation: mechanical only (both ligands are oxidation/acid sensitive)
operating_window.deposition_rate: similar to sulfite at matched CD (high efficiency) [ESTIMATE: medium]
operating_window.anode: platinized Ti/MMO; thiosulfate is anodically fragile — membrane anode compartment strongly preferred, or sacrificial ligand feed schedule [ESTIMATE: published practice, medium]

solutions.maintenance: Watch for: sulfur codeposition (deposit darkens/embrittles — additive/ligand-ratio fault), colloidal sulfur haze (thiosulfate breakdown — bath endpoint), sulfide odor = decomposition. Analysis burden higher than plain sulfite (two ligands). Commercial availability is thinner than plain sulfite products — mostly electronics-oriented and immersion/electroless gold lines [FACT: market observation, no specific vendor claimed]. For the owner's decorative use, plain stabilized sulfite products are the realistic purchase; mixed-ligand matters mainly as the electroless/immersion-gold route for metallized non-conductors.

solutions.purpose: first adherent flash on activated Ni and contamination shield for the main bath, keeping the line fully cyanide-free

composition.tag: [ESTIMATE: handbook practice, medium — many shops simply strike in the main bath at elevated CD]

solutions.maintenance: sacrificial; dump/reclaim when performance drops. HONESTY NOTE: cyanide-free strikes are genuinely WEAKER at activating difficult/passive surfaces than acid cyanide gold strikes — this is one of the real trade-offs of a fully cyanide-free line; compensate with impeccable Ni activation timing (gold within seconds-to-a-minute of fresh Ni) and Wood's strike on stainless [FACT: recognized trade-off].

prep_chain_required: 1. Solvent/ultrasonic alkaline soak degrease — steel wire arrives in drawing lubricant; organics = water-break = zero adhesion.
2. Alkaline electroclean (anodic or periodic-reverse on steel) — strips residual films; anodic mode avoids H-charging and smut.

3. Rinse; acid pickle 10-30 vol% HCl (mild steel) or Wood's nickel strike (stainless: NiCl2 ~240 g/L + HCl ~120 ml/L class) — deoxidize/activate; passive stainless takes nothing without Wood's [FACT].

4. Nickel barrier 2-5 um (bright Ni for leveling; sulfamate Ni if post-plate forming is planned — MORE relevant here than in the hard-gold file because soft sulfite gold can survive gentle forming) — blocks Fe diffusion, pore corrosion, gives leveled premium-looking base. EN 1811 Ni-release limits apply to skin-contact jewelry [FACT: regulation exists].
5. THOROUGH rinse — acid drag-in is the #1 sulfite-bath killer (pH crash -> SO2 + gold precipitation); stricter rinse discipline than cyanide lines.
6. Immediate transfer to gold strike / main bath while Ni is fresh (seconds-to-a-minute) — cyanide-free strikes forgive passive Ni less than cyanide strikes do.
7. Main sulfite gold plate — the process of this file.
NOTE: form-first is still the default flow, but see deposit_properties — soft sulfite gold is the ONE gold deposit class with a real (limited) plate-then-form allowance.

deposit_properties.purity_karat: 99.9%+ Au for undoped sulfite gold — true 24k class, ASTM B488 Type III; As/Sb/Tl-hardened variants remain 99.5%+ (dopant is ppm-to-0.1% level) [FACT: published class structure]
deposit_properties.hardness_HV: undoped soft sulfite gold ~60-100 HV (ASTM B488 Code A/B class); As-doped hardened sulfite gold ~120-160 HV [FACT: published typical ranges]. HONEST COMPARISON: even hardened sulfite gold generally sits at or below the 130-200 HV of Co-hardened acid cyanide hard gold — for a scratch-resistant premium ring surface, cyanide-free costs you wear performance or forces thickness/topcoat compensation.
deposit_properties.thickness_per_pass: 0.1-5 um practical; sulfite deposits are LOW-STRESS (a genuine strength — thick deposits crack less than stressed hard gold), electronics routinely plates multi-um sulfite gold bumps [FACT: published characteristic]; jewelry heavy-wear target 2.5-5 um in one run
deposit_properties.color_control: rich 24k yellow (1N-2N class vicinity, purer/warmer than Co-hard gold's tone); color is stable because deposit is essentially pure Au — LESS color drift risk than hardener-dependent acid gold [FACT: mechanism]; alloyed colors (rose/green) are not this bath's job — separate alloy processes.
deposit_properties.ductility_forming_notes: THE PLATE-THEN-FORM ANSWER, CYANIDE-FREE EDITION: undoped sulfite gold is high-purity, fine-grained, LOW-STRESS and DUCTILE (elongation several %, like wrought pure gold) — it is the most post-formable electrodeposited gold class [FACT: published characteristic]. Gentle bending of plated wire into rings CAN survive over a ductile sulfamate-Ni barrier, unlike brittle Co/Ni-hardened acid gold which microcracks. Hard limits: (a) the Ni barrier and steel core still crack/craze the stack at sharp radii — generous bend radius, ductile Ni, and post-form inspection are mandatory; (b) soft gold scratches easily in service, so plate-then-form buys forming freedom by SPENDING wear resistance; (c) As-hardened sulfite variants lose most of this ductility. Realistic product logic: EITHER form-first + hardened/thicker gold for wear, OR plate-then-form with soft sulfite gold + accept a softer surface (or add a topcoat/final hard flash after forming).

testing_acceptance.acceptance: meets declared class (e.g. >=2.5 um on ring wear zones), 3+ points incl. high-wear areas

no peel at 180-degree own-diameter mandrel bend; soft sulfite gold should bend WITHOUT cracking (unlike hard gold) — cracking here indicates contamination/embrittlement (e.g. sulfur codeposition in thiosulfate variants) and is a reject

testing_acceptance.acceptance: pore count within class for thickness; porosity falls steeply above ~1-2 um
Code A/B (soft, <=90 HK25) for undoped; verify hardened variant hits its TDS window (~120-160 HV class)
As/Tl within declared ppm class; MANDATORY absence check for any food-contact ambition

testing_acceptance.test: nickel release (skin-contact items with Ni barrier)
testing_acceptance.standard_class: EN 1811 (EU REACH: 0.5 ug/cm2/week articles, 0.2 piercing) [FACT: regulation]
testing_acceptance.acceptance: below limit after EN 12472 simulated wear — send-out lab before EU sales

testing_acceptance.standard_class: defined rub/pencil-hardness class vs in-house retained standard
testing_acceptance.acceptance: no base-metal exposure at agreed cycles — set expectations LOWER than hard-gold class for soft deposits, or gate the product on it

testing_acceptance.standard_class: visual vs retained panel; spectrophotometer Lab* if available
testing_acceptance.acceptance: delta within tolerance vs master; sulfite gold should be very stable — drift signals contamination

defects_and_remedies.defect: bath spontaneously darkens, purple/brown colloid, gold mirror on tank/heater, falling Au analysis
defects_and_remedies.cause: THE signature sulfite failure: Au(I) disproportionation — low free sulfite, pH drop, overheating, gold fines seeding, stabilizer depletion
defects_and_remedies.remedy: titrate and restore free sulfite, correct pH up, filter hard (remove every particle), strip plated-out gold, dose stabilizer per TDS; if runaway: reclaim gold and remake — budgeted event, not a surprise

defects_and_remedies.defect: sudden gold precipitation + pungent gas after pretreatment transfer
defects_and_remedies.cause: acid drag-in from pickle line (local pH crash; SO2 release)
defects_and_remedies.remedy: double counterflow rinse before gold; never share tools/racks between acid line and gold without rinse; SO2 = ventilate and step away, then correct pH

defects_and_remedies.cause: passive Ni before gold (sat too long), water-break contamination, no live entry, missing Wood's strike on stainless
defects_and_remedies.remedy: re-activate Ni (dilute acid dip + rinse) and gold within a minute; enforce water-break test; live entry always

defects_and_remedies.cause: heavy-metal contamination (Cu/Pb/Fe ppm), stabilizer/brightener imbalance, temperature or pH out of window
defects_and_remedies.remedy: analyze, dummy-plate at low CD to drag out metallics [ESTIMATE: standard practice], correct additives per TDS, recalibrate pH/T

defects_and_remedies.defect: brittle or dark deposit from a thiosulfate/mixed bath, sulfide smell
defects_and_remedies.remedy: restore sulfite antioxidant excess and ligand ratio; if colloidal sulfur haze persists, bath is at end of life — reclaim

defects_and_remedies.cause: gold fines in suspension (micro-decomposition) — more common than in cyanide baths
defects_and_remedies.remedy: continuous 1-5 um filtration including idle periods; eliminate dust ingress (lid); smooth tank surfaces

defects_and_remedies.cause: CD above limiting for Au content/agitation — sulfite windows are LOWER-CD than users expect coming from other chemistries
defects_and_remedies.remedy: recalculate area, drop current toward 0.2-0.4 A/dm2, increase mechanical agitation, replenish Au

defects_and_remedies.defect: soft gold scratches/drag-marks visible on finished rings
defects_and_remedies.cause: not a bath fault: intrinsic softness of pure sulfite gold + careless post-plate handling
defects_and_remedies.remedy: plastic tweezers/tissue handling, individual packaging; product-level fix: hardened variant, thicker deposit, form-first + final hard flash, or accept satin finish

defects_and_remedies.defect: short bath life / cost per litre-turnover worse than expected
defects_and_remedies.cause: inherent chemistry: sulfite oxidation (air + anode) and slow decomposition even at rest
defects_and_remedies.remedy: lid, mechanical-not-air agitation, cool idle storage, membrane anode if scaling up, size bath small to throughput, and ACCOUNT bath replacement as consumable — this is the honest price of dropping cyanide [FACT: recognized limitation]

defects_and_remedies.defect: steel rusting through gold after weeks
defects_and_remedies.cause: porous thin gold, thin/no Ni barrier — Au cathodic vs steel accelerates pore corrosion [FACT: mechanism]
defects_and_remedies.remedy: Ni barrier 2-5 um mandatory + >=1-2 um Au on wear items + porosity acceptance test

cost_drivers: gold inventory in solution (10 L at 8 g/L = 80 g Au before the first part) — same entry-cost dominance as any gold bath

BATH LIFE: the defining cyanide-free cost delta — sulfite baths die (oxidation + disproportionation) in fewer metal-turnovers than cyanide baths; reclaim recovers the gold but chemistry, labor and downtime recur [FACT: recognized limitation]
proprietary stabilizer/replenisher packages — you are locked to the supplier's system more tightly than with cyanide chemistry
continuous filtration consumables (runs even when idle)
free-sulfite analysis and feed (titration kit or lab)
gold per piece: ~5 cm2 ring at 2.5 um ~ 24 mg Au — deposit cost small; drag-out and bath death dominate losses
near-100% cathode efficiency = faster um/min at matched CD than acid hard gold — a small real cost/time WIN for the cyanide-free side
nickel barrier line — fixed cost of steel substrates, identical to cyanide route

waste: NO cyanide destruction/compliance burden (the headline saving for a home shop), but As/Tl-doped baths re-import serious hazmat cost — undoped soft gold keeps waste genuinely mild (gold-bearing sulfite waste to reclaimer)
insoluble anode upkeep; membrane anode compartment if scaling
XRF access; EN 1811 send-out for EU skin-contact sales

hazards: sulfite and thiosulfate salts release toxic SO2 gas on contact with acid [FACT]
ammonium gold sulfite / ammoniacal baths release ammonia vapor at high pH and temperature [FACT]
arsenic-compound grain refiners (hardened variants): Carc. 1A, acutely toxic; thallium dopants: acutely toxic, cumulative poison [FACT]
amine-class stabilizers/brighteners: typically corrosive/skin-sensitizing class [FACT: class-level; specifics per SDS]
pretreatment line unchanged: HCl pickle corrosive, alkaline electrocleaners corrosive, H2/O2 mist [FACT]
nickel barrier chemistry: Ni salts Carc. class + the #1 contact allergen [FACT]
NO cyanide anywhere in the gold line — the entire acute-lethality tier of the cyanide route is designed out [FACT]
controls: physical acid/gold segregation still binding — not for HCN now, but SO2 + bath-crash: same discipline, different reason
choose UNDOPED soft-gold products to keep the line genuinely low-hazard; treat any As/Tl-hardened product as a hazmat upgrade decision, not a casual add-on
ventilation over tanks (SO2/NH3 potential); lidded tanks double as exposure and bath-life control
nitrile gloves, goggles, apron; no food; wash-up discipline; SDS binder
buy commercial ready-made cyanide-free solution + replenisher with TDS — do not self-compound gold sulfite from gold salts [strong recommendation]

waste: gold-bearing spent bath and drag-out to a precious-metal reclaimer (asset, not just waste); keep Ni line waste separate (aquatic-toxic, regulated); local discharge rules [UNKNOWN — needs local regulation check]
safety.waste: Undoped sulfite gold waste is the mildest waste stream of any gold-plating route: no cyanide destruction step, gold recovers easily (its instability helps). Still: never acidify sulfite waste (SO2); ship gold-bearing streams to a reclaimer; As/Tl-doped bath waste is hazardous waste, full stop; Ni barrier waste regulated separately.

diy_feasibility.verdict: YES — and this is THE default recommendation for a home/DIY shop, which is exactly why hobby and small-jewelry plating suppliers sell mainly cyanide-free sulfite products: it removes cyanide possession, HCN scenarios and cyanide-waste compliance from a residential setting entirely. The honest price: (1) softer deposit than Co-hardened cyanide gold — the scratch-resistant-premium goal needs thickness (2.5-5 um), a hardened variant (which re-imports As-class hazmat), or a final hard topcoat; (2) shorter bath life and fussier bath care (filtration, sulfite titration, acid-drag-in paranoia) — budget bath replacement as a consumable; (3) weaker strike behavior demands tighter Ni-activation timing. For the plate-then-form question, soft sulfite gold is uniquely the FRIENDLIEST gold deposit — the only route where gentle post-plate forming of wire is defensible.
diy_feasibility.minimum_viable_setup: 1-2 L commercial cyanide-free sulfite gold bath + replenisher (undoped soft gold to start), bench CC supply 0-3 A, platinized-Ti anode, lidded PP tank, lab heater, magnetic stirrer (NO air agitation), pH meter, iodometric sulfite test kit or supplier kit, 1-5 um filter loop, drag-out jar, separate degrease/pickle/bright-or-sulfamate-Ni mini-line (non-optional for steel), XRF via service lab initially. Gold-in-solution is the dominant entry cost; hardware modest. [ESTIMATE: setup class, high confidence on component list, no invented prices]
diy_feasibility.hard_limits: cannot match hard-gold wear class without re-importing hazmat (As/Tl) or adding process steps; bath WILL age/die regardless of care — small bath sized to throughput is the only mitigation; cannot plate non-conductive glass without metallization (mixed-ligand electroless/immersion gold is the cyanide-free seed-layer route once metallized); EN 1811 Ni-release testing still required for EU skin-contact sales; food-contact status of stabilizer/dopant residues [UNKNOWN — needs regulation check]; supplier lock-in on proprietary stabilizer packages is structural
